newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour omits rail renationalistaion pledge.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour omits rail renationalistaion pledge.

text.p: Britain's main opposition Labour party said on Thursday it would establish more effective regulation of Britain's railways, but made no mention in its manifesto for the May 1 election of plans to renationalise the network.
The manifesto said rail privatisation had been a poor deal for the taxpayer. It had fragmented the network and was now threatening services.
"Our task will be to improve the situation as we find it, not as we wish it to be," Labour said.

It said its overriding goal must be to win more passengers and get more freight onto rail. The system must be run in the public interest with higher levels of investment and effective enforcement of train operators' service commitments.

"To acheive these aims, we will establish more effective and accountable regulation by the rail regulator; we will ensure that the public subsidy serves the public interest and we will establish a new rail authority, combining functions currently carried out by the rail franchiser and the Department of Transport, to provide a clear, coherent and strategic programme for the development of the railways," the manifesto said.
